entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Caesarius of Arles (b. 470 CE, Chalon-sur-Saône) was a renowned Roman official and jurist of the Classical era, active in Chalon-sur-Saône and later in Arles, Gaul (modern-day France).

As a prominent figure in the Western Roman Empire, Caesarius played a crucial role in the development of Roman law and governance, contributing to the codification of the Lex Romana.

His significance extends beyond his administrative accomplishments, as he was also a key figure in the early Christian Church, serving as a bishop and a mentor to several prominent early Christian leaders.

Despite his importance, Caesarius's legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by that of his contemporaries, and his contributions to Roman law and early Christianity remain an essential part of historical record.

Caesarius's impact on the Western Roman Empire's governance and early Christian Church laid the groundwork for the development of modern Western legal systems and Christian theology.
